qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Mariusz Kamiński (ECR) Subject:

More than a decade since the Political Dialogue and Cooperation Agreement with Cuba was signed, it has become clear that it serves only the communist regime, legitimises its continued existence and provides funds to corrupt regime apparatchiks. The EU’s inexplicable attitude, which fails to recognise Havana’s open violation of all its commitments, as I have repeatedly pointed out to the High Representative1, is opposed by the European Parliament2. In the European Parliament – alongside representatives of the Cuban opposition and Ukrainian intelligence services – I have presented facts proving that communist Cuba is the main source of mercenaries in Russia’ war of aggression against Ukraine3. This will be clearly stated in the resolution that the European Parliament will adopt on the fourth anniversary of Russia’s war of aggression. The regime’s attitude is therefore openly hostile towards Europe. Analyses, which should also be known to the EEAS, show that Havana is strengthening its military cooperation with Belarus4. Lithuania has issued arrest warrants for Cuban citizens who have committed acts of sabotage on EU territory5. By feigning ignorance of these facts, the EU is undermining our security. Equally disastrous are the PDCA’s ‘achievements’ within Cuba. In 2025, political repression intensified and the number of political prisoners rose to 1 1976. While the regime survives solely through repression, the EU is spending EUR 3 million on the ‘Digital Cuba’ project7. The Estonian Government, whose companies are to supply the regime with digital equipment and solutions, has recognised the scandalous nature of this policy8. 1.

Does the EU – contrary to the obvious facts, the interests of Cubans and European security – intend to maintain the shameful existence of the PDCA and pursue its scandalous policy of cooperation with communist Havana until the regime collapses?
Was this issue discussed at the January Foreign Affairs Council meeting?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.5.2026) EU engagement with Cuba is guided by its values and interests. Since 2017, the EU/Cuba Political Dialogue and Cooperation Agreement1 (PDCA), agreed by the European Parliament and Member States, has been the basic framework for EU/Cuba relations. The Agreement is not a way to ignore differences, but a way to address them including sensitive topics such as human rights on the island and Cuba’s position in relation to the Russian war of aggression against Ukraine. The Agreement, through an increased critical but constructive engagement, is expected to deliver further and more concrete results. The best possible option to achieve this goal is to make its implementation and working methods more effective, rather than to abandon it. It is currently analysing ways towards this end, in order that the PDCA can better respond to expectations in promoting reforms, encouraging human rights, and supporting Cuba’s economic and social modernisation, while protecting European interests, including EU’s security. In relation to EU cooperation, including humanitarian relief, it aims at enhancing the well-being of Cuban citizens. EU funds are not transmitted to the Cuban authorities. EU-funded projects in Cuba are implemented by United Nations’ agencies, Member States’ agencies and EU nongovernmental organisations. As with all EU cooperation projects worldwide, a variety of tools are used to ensure the proper execution, monitoring and auditing of EU projects in Cuba. Cuba was not a topic of the January 2026 Foreign Affairs Council.
